subject: English
description: The English LDG covers grammar, usage, and language conventions. Many writing difficulties trace to gaps here.

competencies.label: Parts of Speech
competencies.description: Identifying and using nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs in sentences.

misconceptions.observed: Cannot identify the verb in a sentence.
misconceptions.rootGap: Confuses word meaning with word function; e.g. thinks 'run' is always a verb even in 'a morning run.'
misconceptions.evidence: Labels all action words as verbs regardless of sentence role.
misconceptions.strategy: Function-first teaching: 'What job is this word doing in this sentence?' not 'What does this word mean?'

competencies.label: Verb Tenses
competencies.description: Using past, present, and future tenses correctly and consistently.

misconceptions.observed: Switches tenses mid-paragraph: 'She walks to school and then she ate lunch.'
misconceptions.rootGap: Does not understand that tense must be consistent across a narrative.
misconceptions.evidence: Mixes past and present in the same sentence or paragraph.
misconceptions.strategy: Timeline visual; colour-code past/present/future; tense-consistency editing checklist.

competencies.label: Subject-Verb Agreement
competencies.description: Matching the verb form to the subject in number and person.

misconceptions.rootGap: Does not hear or apply the agreement pattern; interference from spoken dialect in some cases.
misconceptions.evidence: Inconsistent agreement, especially with irregular verbs and third-person singular.
misconceptions.strategy: Oral practice before writing; 'He/She/It + s' anchor chart; peer editing for agreement only.

competencies.label: Punctuation
competencies.description: Using full stops, commas, question marks, quotation marks, and apostrophes correctly.

misconceptions.observed: No punctuation at all or random capital letters mid-sentence.
misconceptions.rootGap: Does not understand that punctuation guides the reader; writing is treated as a continuous stream.
misconceptions.evidence: Entire paragraph without a single full stop; capital letters on random words.
misconceptions.strategy: Read writing aloud exactly as punctuated; punctuation hunts in familiar books; 'punctuation police' peer editing.

competencies.label: Sentence Variety
competencies.description: Using simple, compound, and complex sentences for effect.

misconceptions.observed: All sentences start the same way ('I…', 'The…', 'It…'). Writing feels monotonous.
misconceptions.rootGap: Has not learned to vary sentence openings or combine ideas.
misconceptions.evidence: Every sentence is simple; no conjunctions beyond 'and'.
misconceptions.strategy: Sentence combining exercises; teach sentence openers (adverb, prepositional phrase, subordinate clause).
